author: PokerFace
body:
Hi, I'm here with a suggestion.
(Please don't h8 m8)

Anyways, in-game I always see staff saying stuff like Watch the caps!, or like Watch the language! This is fine but, sometimes the players will respond with an insult. Something like this had happened in a game one time. A mod was on and was telling people in that way that all mods do. Something like "Please be more appropriate in chat." Well, it continued for a while. Not saying that I deserve mod or anything but, since they weren't listening to the staff, I decided to jump in. I said something along the lines of "Hey man, your funny but, we gotta keep it appropriate for the kiddos if you know what I mean." Guess what happened, the person actually apologized to me and said "sorry poker." Then, they actually explained themselves and said they were 12 years old and were in "that stage." I was surprised at this. I think if you give a warning more understanding and compassionate of the player, they would be more likely to listen and be respectful. When you say "Watch the caps!" there is no feeling or emotion behind this. If you say something like, "Hey man, could you ease up on the caps" I'm sure that the player would be more likely to listen. 
Example:
Response-Negative
Reaction-Negative

Response-Positive
Reaction-Positive

Please take this into consideration as it has been proven to work. I understand that things should be "Official" but, sometimes it's not the best thing. Thank you! Have a nice day!

replies.author: Howsie
replies.body:
I heartily agree with detty. The fact that this has become an issue is appalling. Let me just take a few lines from what is the most basic criteria required when being a staff member in this community. 

"Have an excellent attitude in general and an easy going person who will be able to communicate with the players and staff well." - COMMUNICATION IS KEY. If you can't effectively communicate yourself to both users and staff you have no place on the staff team. 

"You must be mature and be able to conduct yourself in a polite way." - Maturity DOES NOT mean superiority. You are there to support the users and staff and most important ENJOY YOURSELF while doing it. If you can't do this, leave the staff team. 

"Confident in speaking to people much younger and much older than yourself without making yourself sound superior or inferior." - Once again COMMUNICATION IS KEY. This is all too important in a community that caters to a diverse range of individuals. Once again, if you can't do this effectively (thats right, you guessed it.) divert yourself away from being a member of the avicus staff team.

replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
In my opinion, it's really, really not even that hard to find a balance between stringency and leniency. I'm sure it's a putative belief that players oftentimes become substantially more austere and robotic after being promoted to a staff position. Generally, these people are the ones who end up being poor, injudicious moderators; there's nothing natural or hospitable about someone who unemotionally says "watch the caps" dozens of times in succession with no regard to what's going on behind the text on their screen. It's apathetic, lazy, and supercilious. A good staff member has the "people's touch" and can effectively connect with other players, assertively when called for, in a casual and sensible manner. I thought having this demeanor was a prerequisite for being a junior moderator. Apparently not.

In other words, if you're a staff member and can't enforce rules in a pragmatic and friendly manner, then you don't deserve such a position. It's seriously just common sense, which unfortunately is very hard to come by nowadays.

Also, I love how the original post calls this a "suggestion" when this is how the staff should be acting routinely anyway; what's more, people are actually glorifying this as a "good idea" of sorts, as if this thread isn't merely someone recommending something that goes without saying. That... really says a lot about the community and how rudimentary we are.

replies.author: Y0urm0m1
replies.body:
This is my opinion on this subject so no h8 pls.

It is good to be casual but also be assertive at the same time. IT is a bit hard to do but it is something you will learn in time. The staff should always try to connect with the player / community. Just because you are staff, doesn't mean your higher up or necassarly gods. There shouldn't be a barrier. You choose to become staff because you want to help the server. the staff should interact with the community, get in touch with them and relate. I agree on almost every single points.

However, the downside to it is if the staff says something like that, chances are they might take it as a mere joke and still continue to do it. "you can lead a horse to water but can't make it drink". The staff can be nice and casual about this but in the end, its up to them to make the decision. If there is no firm grip on them, they would disregard the warning and continue rulebreaking.

To conclude, there should be a balance. While it is good to be casual about the situation, there is also a time on assertiveness. Staff shouldn't be to casual/ lenient nor they should be to harsh or strict. The goal of the staff team of Avicus is to make this community/ server an enjoyable place for everyone. This is the staff's responsibility to keep and they must keep it. This is like an important fundemental so keep it this in mind. I trust that the staff team are entitlied to their own decisions and choices in order to make Avicus an enjoyable place to play on.
